features.name: ordinal_group1_avg
features.description: Average of the first sequence of ordinal variables (a1 to a5).
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a smooth, continuous composite score that helps the linear SVM establish a stable margin based on the overall level of the first ordinal group.

features.name: ordinal_group2_avg
features.description: Average of the second sequence of ordinal variables (a6 to a10).
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a smooth, continuous composite score for the second ordinal group, useful for linear combinations and margin boundaries.

features.name: ordinal_group_diff
features.description: Difference between the averages of the two ordinal groups.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the relative shift between the two ordinal sequences, allowing the SVM to weight the divergence directly.

features.name: continuous_group1_log_sum
features.description: Log-transformed sum of the first sequence of continuous variables (a11 to a15).
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalizes the skewed continuous sum into a smoother, more linear space, preventing large outliers from dominating the SVM margin.

features.name: continuous_group2_log_sum
features.description: Log-transformed sum of the second sequence of continuous variables (a16 to a20).
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalizes the magnitude of the second continuous group, providing a well-scaled feature for linear projection.

features.name: continuous_group_ratio
features.description: Ratio of the sums of the two continuous variable groups, with a small constant to prevent division by zero.
features.expected_model_benefit: Exposes the proportional relationship between the two continuous sequences, which is often a strong linear separator when absolute magnitudes vary.

features.name: continuous_tail_diff
features.description: Difference between the final values of the two continuous sequences (a15 and a20).
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights the divergence at the end of the continuous sequences, providing a direct linear feature for the SVM to split on.

features.name: ordinal_tail_diff
features.description: Difference between the final values of the two ordinal sequences (a5 and a10).
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the endpoint divergence of the ordinal sequences, useful for fine-tuning the linear decision boundary.

features.name: continuous_spread_group1
features.description: The spread or range of the first continuous sequence, calculated as the difference between its last and first elements.
features.expected_model_benefit: Measures the internal growth or decay within the first continuous sequence, offering a slope-like feature for the linear model.

features.name: continuous_spread_group2
features.description: The spread or range of the second continuous sequence, calculated as the difference between its last and first elements.
features.expected_model_benefit: Measures the internal growth or decay within the second continuous sequence, complementing the first spread feature.

features.name: ordinal_progression_consistency
features.description: Semantic judgment of how consistently the ordinal values increase from a1 to a5 and a6 to a10, scored as a continuous severity measure.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a non-linear pattern assessment transformed into a continuous score, allowing the linear SVM to utilize complex sequence behaviors.

features.name: continuous_magnitude_category
features.description: Semantic judgment categorizing the overall magnitude and volatility of the continuous variables into a continuous severity score.
features.expected_model_benefit: Translates complex multi-variable interactions into a single, smooth severity dimension that is highly compatible with linear margin optimization.
